summary.headline: Max Healthcare Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR 3,219 crore, with operating EBITDA up 18% to INR 820 crore at a 26.8% margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 20% YoY and 8% QoQ to INR 3,219 crore, while operating EBITDA rose 18% YoY to INR 820 crore and PAT rose 10% YoY to INR 448 crore. Occupancy held at 77% despite a 14% increase in operational beds, as 202 brownfield beds were added in the quarter. Management attributed the Saket complex EBITDA drag to ramp-up of the newly commissioned Max Smart beds, and said oncology revenue fell after CGHS-driven chemotherapy discontinuation. Management said it has not yet quantified the impact of the new trade margin cap on non-scheduled drugs.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 2,384 crore at end-June 2026; net debt/EBITDA below 1x
INR 292 crore to capex, INR 195 crore to dividend

segments.name: Hospital network
segments.commentary: Occupancy 77% on ~14% higher operational beds; total bed capacity ~6,200 (+20% YoY). Oncology share of IP revenue fell to 21% from 26%; ex-oncology gross revenue grew 25% and ARPP grew 11% YoY.

segments.name: Max@Home
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 86 crore, +37% YoY; 16 service lines across 15 cities; over 56% repeat transactions.

segments.name: Max Lab
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 66 crore, +24% YoY; services in over 60 cities; served over 7 lakh patients in the quarter.

segments.name: Max Bhubaneswar (Kalinga Hospital, 66% owned)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 38 crore and EBITDA INR 4 crore; renovation of ~80 beds under way, first part of the renovation delivered in about 3 months, and a 250-bed phased renovation over 12 to 15 months.

guidance_outlook: Max Smart (Saket) remaining 140 beds to be commissioned after Diwali; balance 205 beds at Max Nanavati and Max Smart to open post Diwali; management expects Saket EBITDA drag to normalise by the next quarter.

Overall oncology revenue impact from CGHS-linked chemotherapy discontinuation was roughly INR 100 crore a year, against a net gain of about INR 200 crore from CGHS price revisions; management said the revenue decline is now anniversarying from Q3 FY27, so top-line growth should accelerate in Q3 and Q4.
Gurugram Sector-56 (500 beds): phased commissioning to start by end of FY27; initial 150-200 beds; peak EBITDA loss estimated at INR 40-50 crore; breakeven targeted within about one year.
Zirakpur, Mohali (400 beds): commissioning by December 2027; peak EBITDA loss around INR 30 crore, a 'line in the sand' estimate.
Board approved INR 415 crore for 209 brownfield beds at Max Noida, Max Vaishali and BLK-Max, plus an MLCP tower at BLK (~INR 85 crore); most capacity expected over 18 to 24 months.
Trade margin cap on non-scheduled drugs: sales and EBITDA impact still being worked out; the matter is sub judice.
capex_capacity: Q2 added 202 brownfield beds (Max Smart, Max Lucknow, Max Noida, Max Dwarka); Max Dwarka oncology block adds ~20 beds in Q3 FY27.
Max Smart's newly commissioned 260 beds reached EBITDA breakeven within 3 months; 140 beds remain to be commissioned after Diwali.

Pipeline: 100 beds at Max Lucknow over the next 2 quarters; 85 beds at Max Noida and 100 beds at Max Nagpur by December 2027; 200 beds at Pitampura in FY29; 400 beds at Patparganj by end-FY29; 260-bed Dwarka tower, 271-bed Nanavati Phase 2, 450-bed Pune, 200-bed Vaishali Tower 3 and 400-bed Shaheed Path Lucknow Phase 1 by FY30 (Shaheed Path awaiting environmental clearance and building plans).
Greenfield Greater Noida has land for 400 beds only; no operating hospital there. Noida campus: 500-bed complex with 400 active; residual 11 acres can host ~700 beds in a separate phase.
H1 FY27 capex: INR 629 crore on expansion projects and upgrades at new units; INR 386 crore on acquisitions of Kalinga Hospital (Bhubaneswar) and Yerawada Properties (Pune).
demand_pricing: Institutional bed share fell to 29% from 34% a year earlier, supporting ARPP; management said it is not reducing institutional exposure, and older hospitals are de-empanelling while newer ones empanel.

CGHS empanelment: BLK de-empanelled in May from CGHS and Railways for non-payment; ECHS Shalimar Bagh also de-empanelled. Empanelment is a 6-month evergreen contract with 1-month notice from either side; Gurugram new hospital to seek CGHS/ECHS empanelment.
Management said other specialties grew around 20% YoY and occupied bed days have not fallen by specialty.
Management said the sector's median net margin is about 9% and that hospital pricing has been product-based rather than service-based, implying a possible recalibration.
Pharmacy share of revenue was not disclosed; 20-30% of revenue is packaged, depending on payor.

qa_highlights.question: How many hospitals were de-empanelled, and will more follow?
qa_highlights.answer: BLK was de-empanelled from CGHS and Railways in May for non-payment, and ECHS Shalimar Bagh was also de-empanelled. Further decisions will be taken hospital by hospital, with older hospitals reducing institutional mix.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the Saket drag last, and will other brownfields see similar drags?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said brownfields break even within the first quarter, and the Saket drag is a one-quarter ramp-up effect that should normalise by next quarter. Mohali and Nanavati followed the same pattern.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the trade margin cap on sales and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still working out the impact. It said chemotherapy is about 30% of oncology revenue, and some ORC and monopoly drugs are exempt. CGHS impact is already in the numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Gurugram greenfield ramp-up and EBITDA impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will open 150-200 beds first, and that peak EBITDA loss should be around INR 40-50 crore, based on Dwarka's INR 30 crore loss on 300 beds.

qa_highlights.question: Will ex-oncology growth flow through to EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to impute EBITDA ex-oncology. It said the chemotherapy drop cost roughly INR 100 crore a year, offset by a net CGHS gain of about INR 200 crore, and cardiology grew 16%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Max Lab and Max@Home become larger contributors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both have grown around 20-25% CAGR over many years and that their revenue share remains stable while the core grows at about 20%.

risks_watch: Trade margin cap on non-scheduled drugs and pending court matter; impact not yet quantified by management.
Clinician attrition and recruitment for new Gurugram and other greenfield hospitals; management says attrition is about 1% a year.
Greenfield and brownfield drag on EBITDA as new beds ramp up (Gurugram INR 40-50 crore peak loss; Zirakpur ~INR 30 crore).
Pace of oncology revenue recovery in Q3 and Q4 FY27 as the CGHS discontinuation anniversaries.
Bhubaneswar renovation timing and occupancy, and the Kalinga Hospital EBITDA contribution.
Shaheed Path Lucknow Phase 1 is awaiting environmental clearance and building plans, so FY30 timing is at risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics and ramp-up trajectories, but evasive on the trade margin cap, pharmacy mix and EBITDA impact of ex-oncology growth, citing the sub judice matter and bundled billing. Management stressed that brownfield breakeven is quick and that greenfield peak-loss figures are preliminary estimates.
key_quotes: We gained momentum in the second quarter, with revenue growing by 20%, operating EBITDA by 18% and PAT by 10%.
There is a hockey-stick growth curve.
We cannot impute a value which is not there in the P&L.

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth % guided; management says top-line growth should accelerate in Q3 and Q4 as the CGHS oncology decline anniversaries, backed by 140 Saket beds after Diwali, 100 Lucknow beds, and approved 209 brownfield beds (INR 415 crore), with occupancy steady at 77% on 14% more beds.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Operating EBITDA margin 26.8% in Q2 FY27 (up ~200 bps QoQ) and Saket drag expected to normalise next quarter, but greenfield peak losses of INR 40-50 crore (Gurugram) and INR 30 crore (Zirakpur) and unquantified trade margin cap weigh against expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 202 brownfield beds added in Q2, 140 Saket beds after Diwali (Q3 FY27), 20 Dwarka oncology beds in Q3, and Gurugram Sector-56 phased start (150-200 beds) by end FY27; operational beds up 14% YoY.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Occupied bed days up 13% YoY and 7% QoQ; management expects top-line growth to accelerate in Q3 and Q4 as the CGHS oncology decline (~INR 100 crore a year) anniversaries, with occupancy steady at 77%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 77% with 14% more beds, the Board has already approved INR 415 crore for 209 brownfield beds and a ~INR 85 crore MLCP, and a 250-bed Bhubaneswar renovation is under way, so further capex announcements are probable on the pipeline (Pitampura, Patparganj, Pune, Nanavati Phase 2).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No explicit revenue guidance; ex-oncology gross revenue grew 25% YoY and H1 revenue rose 18%, so an acceleration in Q3-Q4 could support upgrades, but management gave no numeric guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Trade margin cap on non-scheduled drugs is unquantified and sub judice, BLK and ECHS Shalimar Bagh de-empanelled, and Saket/greenfield ramp losses (Gurugram INR 40-50 crore peak) could weigh on EBITDA.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Max@Home has 16 service lines and Max Lab serves 60+ cities; new service lines are plausible but no specific launch was named or dated on the call.

rows.label: CGHS anniversary lifts top-line growth
rows.why: CGHS chemotherapy discontinuation cost ~INR 100 crore a year against a net ~INR 200 crore CGHS price-revision gain, and the decline anniversaries from Q3 FY27, so growth should accelerate.

rows.label: Trade margin cap on non-scheduled drugs
rows.why: Sales and EBITDA impact not yet quantified by management; the matter is sub judice, so the outcome is a downside risk to margins and pharmacy revenue.

rows.label: International patient revenue growth
rows.why: International revenue grew 33% YoY to INR 307 crore, 10% of hospital healthcare revenue, which supports mix and ARPP.

tone.note: Management was confident on occupancy, brownfield breakeven and ramp-up, and on CGHS anniversary; it was evasive on the trade margin cap, pharmacy mix and ex-oncology EBITDA, while analysts probed de-empanelments, Saket drag and greenfield losses.
